reference: Nicolaus Cusanus, Cribratio Alkorani, Liber III, cap. V, printed p. 917 (1565 Opera)
gist_en: Argues that the Qur'an's God is a servant of Muhammad's sexual appetite and swears by creatures; a personal attack on Muhammad's conduct.
why_excluded: Personal insult about Muhammad's sexual conduct (exclusion rule: personal insult). The doctrinal core (a God who swears by creatures and contradicts himself) is covered by CU-02 and the Cap. V wording itself is not reproduced in passages.json.

reference: Nicolaus Cusanus, Cribratio Alkorani, Liber III, cap. I-II, printed pp. 915-916 (1565 Opera); also in Paris 1514 print
gist_en: Says the final proof of the Qur'an is the sword: Muhammad told people to fight until they confessed God and himself; those who submitted were saved from slaughter.
why_excluded: Borderline: it reports a Qur'anic command to fight until people testify and calls the sword the Qur'an's 'ultima resolutio'. The point is critical (S theme), but its wording is close to a call to war. Kept out of passages.json; the team may reinstate it under S with the quoted-opponent label if it accepts the S-theme's historical reading.
